summary: This note is a Wikipedia-style biography of Ibrahim Abboud, a Sudanese military officer born in 1900 near Suakin. It traces his training as an engineer, his commissions in the Egyptian Army and then the Sudan Defence Force, and his wartime service in Eritrea, Ethiopia and North Africa. It ends with his rise to commander in chief after Sudanese independence and his leadership of the military government after the November 1958 coup.
one_line: Biography of Ibrahim Abboud, Sudanese army officer who rose to commander in chief and led the military government after the 1958 coup.
key_facts: Ibrahim Abboud was born 26 October 1900 at Mohammed-Gol, near the old port city of Suakin on the Red Sea.
Ibrahim Abboud trained as an engineer at the Gordon Memorial College and at the Military College in Khartoum.
Ibrahim Abboud received a commission in the Egyptian Army in 1918.
Ibrahim Abboud transferred to the Sudan Defence Force in 1925, after its creation separate from the Egyptian army.
During World War II, Ibrahim Abboud served in Eritrea, in Ethiopia, with the Sudan Defence Force, and with the British army in North Africa.
Ibrahim Abboud became commander of the Sudan Defence Force in 1949.
Ibrahim Abboud became assistant commander in chief in 1954.
With the declaration of independence for the Sudan in 1956, Ibrahim Abboud was made commander in chief of the Sudanese military forces.
The Sudanese army staged a "coup d'état" in November 1958, overthrowing the civilian government of Abdullah Khalil.
After the November 1958 coup, Gen. Ibrahim Abboud led the new military government.
